Krest Industrial Technologies02
KIT  /  Brand GuidelinesBrand

Brand
introduction

KIT — Krest Industrial Technologies — designs, integrates and maintains the industrial systems that production depends on. We work across process engineering, automation and industrial data as a single accountable discipline.

Our customers do not buy components. They buy the certainty that a line will run, a tolerance will hold, and a plant will still be performing in year ten.

The brand in one line
We engineer the certainty
that industry runs on.
What we are

An industrial technology company. Not a consultancy, not a distributor, not a software vendor. We take responsibility for the engineered outcome and everything required to reach it.

How we behave

We work to the number. We commit to what we can prove. We say what a system will and will not do, and we stay accountable for it long after commissioning.

Why the identity matters

Consistency is the visible form of reliability. A brand applied with the same discipline as an engineering tolerance tells the market how the company works before a single conversation begins.

Process engineering
Industrial automation
Systems integration
Industrial data
Lifecycle service

KIT  /  Brand GuidelinesBrand

Brand essence

The essence is the fixed point of the brand. Every message, image and application should be traceable back to it.

The four pillars below are the working translation of that essence. They govern what KIT says, and equally what it declines to say.

Brand essence
Engineered certainty
01
Precision

Tolerance is a commitment, not an aspiration. We work to the measured number and we publish it.

02
Systems thinking

Nothing is specified in isolation. Every component is designed for the system it will live inside for a decade.

03
Reliability

Performance is judged in year five, not week one. Uptime is the only metric that survives contact with a factory floor.

04
Scale

What holds on one line holds across a plant, a network and a continent. Repeatability is the product.

Identity
elements

The KIT identity has two approved elements and no others. The supplied artwork is the single source of truth: the marks are never redrawn, re-set from a font, traced or rebuilt.

The primary expression is the lockup on KIT Navy, with the metallic wordmark. Every other version answers a constraint that prevents it.

Full corporate lockup Primary

The default in every context that allows a dark ground: covers, signage, stationery, first screens, tender documents, presentation masters and vehicle livery.

Lockup on light Alternate

Used where a dark ground is not available or not appropriate — long-form documents, technical specifications, third-party templates and partner material.

Wordmark Secondary

Used once the corporate name is established in the same view, and in constrained formats: app icons, avatars, machinery plates, apparel, embossing.

There is no standalone symbol. The accent is never extracted from the i.

Logo anatomy

The wordmark is a drawn form, not typography. Its details are deliberate, and they are what keep the mark recognisable at small size and in low-fidelity reproduction.

All values are measured from the supplied master artwork. x denotes the vertical stem weight; H denotes the cap height.

Cap lineBaselineCrossbar 0.99xAccent terminatesStem beginsTangent vertex 0.49HInk box 10.29x × 4.22x
01
Cap height H

The shared height of K, i and T. H = 4.22x and is the clear-space unit for the whole system.

02
Stem weight x

The vertical stem of the K and T. This is the base construction unit; every other dimension is a multiple of it.

03
Tangent vertex

The arm and leg of the K converge and meet the stem at the vertical midpoint of the cap height.

04
The accent

The upper segment of the i bar, in flat KIT Gold. The bar is one continuous full-height form, not a letter with a separate dot.

05
The cut

Three parallel diagonals at 44° divide the i bar; the K arm and leg run at 45°.

06
The descriptor

Two centred lines of bold uppercase. KREST INDUSTRIAL takes the wordmark colour; TECHNOLOGIES is always gold.

07
The gradient

The wordmark and the first descriptor line carry a vertical gradient. It is part of the artwork — see page 11.

Clear space

Clear space is measured in H — the cap height of the KIT wordmark, taken from the baseline to the top of the K. It is the only unit used, and it scales with the mark.

Minimum clear space is 1H on all four sides of the artwork bounding box. Nothing enters this zone: no type, no rule, no image edge, no other logo, no page trim.

Full corporate lockup
1H1H1H1H
Wordmark
1H1H1H1H
Defining the unit

H is the cap height of the wordmark — 4.22x, where x is the stem weight. Because H is read directly off the artwork, clear space is correct at any scale without recalculation.

Constrained exception

In fixed interface furniture — application bars, browser tabs, embedded video overlays — clear space may reduce to 0.5H. This is the only permitted reduction, and it does not apply to print, signage or partner materials.

Measure from the ink

Clear space is measured from the outer edge of the artwork, not the file boundary. Supplied masters carry no built-in padding; if a file has been re-exported with margins, re-measure from the ink.

Minimum size

Minimum sizes are set by the descriptor, which fails before the wordmark does. Below these values the lockup stops working and the wordmark is used on its own.

The gradient also has a floor. Below 20 mm the ramp is no longer legible as a finish and the monochrome versions are used instead.

Actual size — full corporate lockup
Recommended  44 mm

Comfortable — use wherever space allows

Minimum  32 mm

Absolute floor for print

Unacceptable  21 mm

Descriptor illegible — use the wordmark instead

The switch point

When available width falls below 32 mm in print or 130 px on screen, do not scale the lockup further. Change element: use the wordmark on its own and carry the corporate name in the surrounding typography.

KIT  /  Brand GuidelinesLogo

Logo variations

Four master files cover every reproduction condition. There are no other approved versions, and new ones are not created locally.

The two gradient versions are always preferred. Monochrome is a response to a production constraint, never a stylistic choice.

Primary — on Navy Primary

Metallic wordmark, flat gold TECHNOLOGIES, Light Grey KREST INDUSTRIAL. Use on KIT Navy and Deep Charcoal.

On light grounds Alternate

Blue-to-Navy wordmark and first descriptor line, with the gold second line. Use on white, KIT Paper and Light Grey.

Monochrome — white Constrained

Single-colour reverse. Photography, dark substrates, single-pass print and any process that cannot hold a gradient.

Monochrome — Navy Constrained

Single-colour positive. One-colour print, engraving, etching, moulding and fax-grade reproduction.

File formats

SVG, EPS and PDF hold the gradient as vector and are the masters. PNG with transparency for presentation and document templates. No JPEG masters — the format cannot hold a transparent ground.

Naming

KIT_lockup_dark, KIT_lockup_light, KIT_lockup_mono-white, KIT_lockup_mono-navy — and the matching KIT_wordmark_* set. Do not rename or re-version locally.

Never generate a new variation

If a situation appears to need a version that does not exist — a different accent colour, an outlined mark, a re-angled gradient, a single-line descriptor — the answer is a different application, not a new logo file.

The wordmark carries a vertical gradient across the cap height. It is the most distinctive feature of the mark and the one most often reproduced incorrectly.

Both gradients are built entirely from the core palette. Neither introduces a new hue, and neither is ever re-created by hand — they are held in the master artwork.

Logo and
colour

The logo is placed on flat brand colour or on white. Contrast between the mark and its ground is the only criterion, and it is measured rather than judged by eye.

The metallic version belongs on dark grounds and the tonal version on light. Swapping them is the single most common error in the system.

KIT Gold is its counterweight: a controlled accent that signals precision. It appears inside the mark itself, and sparingly everywhere else.

Colour
accessibility

Every text and background pair is verified against WCAG 2.1 contrast ratios before use. Body copy must reach 4.5:1; text at 24pt or above, and bold text at 18.5pt or above, may sit at 3:1.

Ratios are printed beside each pair so they can be checked rather than assumed. The combinations on the lower row are not permitted for text at any size.

Colour misuse

Colour is the fastest way to weaken the identity, because it degrades quietly. These are the failures that occur most often in practice.

Where a tint is needed, take it from the extended palette on page 16. Never approximate a brand colour by eye, and never rely on opacity to produce one.

×Do not introduce colours outside the palette
×Do not use gradients as brand surfaces — the identity gradient belongs to the wordmark alone
Precision at scale
×Do not set type in low-contrast pairs
Gold is an accent. It is never a ground for body copy, and never the dominant colour in a layout.
×Do not use Gold as a reading surface
Uptimeengineeredin
×Do not use multiple text colours in one line
×Do not let Gold dominate a composition
×Do not darken, lighten or tint core colours by eye
×Do not apply opacity to brand colours — use a defined tint
Specify, don't sample

Never pick a colour from a screenshot, a PDF or a photograph. Take values from this document or the supplied swatch libraries.

Opacity is not a tint

A colour at 45% opacity changes with whatever sits behind it and will not reproduce in print. Use the fixed tint values instead.

Check the ratio

Any new colour pairing is measured before it ships. If it does not reach 4.5:1 for body copy, it is not used, regardless of how it looks.

KIT  /  Brand GuidelinesTypography

Typeface
system

IBM Plex Sans is the KIT typeface. It was drawn for an engineering company, it carries a complete weight range, and its licence permits use across print, web, product interface and embedded systems without per-seat cost.

IBM Plex Mono handles anything that is measured: figures, part numbers, tolerances, labels and code. The two share proportions, so they set together without adjustment.

Where Mono is used

Measurements, tolerances, part and drawing numbers, serial numbers, timestamps, code, table figures, section labels and page numbers.

The logo is not typography

The descriptor — KREST INDUSTRIAL TECHNOLOGIES — is drawn artwork, not Plex. Never re-set it, and never use Plex to extend or replace it.

Substitution

Where Plex cannot be installed — third-party systems, email clients, customer templates — substitute Arial (Sans) and Consolas (Mono). Never Times, never Calibri, never a display face.

Typographic
hierarchy

The scale is fixed. Sizes below are set for A4 print; on screen, multiply by 1.33 and round to the nearest whole pixel.

Tracking is negative on large sizes and positive on small ones. Never track body copy, and never justify it — KIT text is always set ragged right.

Measure

Body copy runs between 55 and 75 characters per line. Below 45 the text fragments; above 85 the eye loses the return.

Alignment

Always ragged right. Justification creates rivers and forces hyphenation, both of which read as carelessness in a technical document.

Baseline grid

All text sits on a 4 mm baseline grid. Headings occupy whole multiples so columns align across a spread regardless of their content.

Emphasis

Use weight, not italic. Plex Sans Medium or SemiBold carries emphasis; italics are reserved for publication titles and Latin abbreviations.

Never

No outlines, no all-caps body copy, no letter-spaced lower case, no drop shadows, no stretching or condensing to fit. If it does not fit, edit the words.

KIT  /  Brand GuidelinesGraphic system

Graphic language

The KIT graphic language is drawn out of the logo, not applied to it. Every element below traces back to a measurement in the mark: the 45° cut, the bar proportion, the modular grid.

Used sparingly, these five elements are enough to make any layout recognisable without a logo present. Used decoratively, they become noise.

The Cut

The 45° diagonal that governs the K and the cuts in the i. Used for image crops, section transitions and rule terminals. One angle only.

The Datum Grid

A visible engineering grid at the page module. Marks alignment and structure; sits behind content at low contrast, never over it.

Nodes and Paths

Square nodes on straight paths at 45° or 90°. Represents systems, connection and process flow without resorting to circuitry clichés.

The Bar

Derived from the proportion of the i bar (1 : 4.22). The unit for data visualisation and section markers.

The Measure

A technical scale rule with major and minor ticks. Used along page edges and as a datum for figures. A single gold marker indicates the value in question.

One system, one angle

45° and 90° are the only angles in the KIT system, taken straight from the mark. Any other angle is a mistake, not a variation.

Structure, not ornament

A graphic element earns its place by organising information. If it can be removed without losing meaning, remove it.

Never

No circuit boards, no glowing networks, no neural diagrams, no isometric city grids, no particle fields, no 3D renders of abstract data.

Graphic elements
in application

The elements are applied at three intensities. Structural use organises a page; accent use marks a single point; atmospheric use fills a dark field at very low contrast.

Only one intensity is used per surface. A page with an atmospheric grid does not also carry structural rules and node paths.

Structural
Four plants.
One control system.

Rules divide, the grid aligns, the accent marks the entry point.

Hairlines and the datum grid carry the layout. Use on white and Paper grounds for documents and technical content.

KIT  /  Brand GuidelinesGraphic system

Iconography

Icons are drawn on a 24-unit grid with a 20-unit live area. Stroke weight is a constant 1.6 units and never scales independently of the icon.

Corners are square, terminals are butt-cut, and geometry is restricted to 90° and 45°. No rounded joints, no filled shapes, no two-tone icons, no gradients.

Imagery

KIT photography is documentary, not staged. It shows real plant, real components and real people working, shot with the discipline of an architectural photographer.

Frames on this page are placement guides, not images. They describe the brief for each slot; final photography is commissioned and held in the KIT asset library.

Subject direction
Photography Advanced manufacturing floor — wide, low, symmetrical
Photography Precision component, macro — machined surface and tolerance
Photography Engineer at a control station — concentration, not eye contact
Photography Automation cell in motion — long exposure, controlled blur
Photography Material detail — steel, alloy, composite under raking light
Photography Plant at scale — exterior, dusk, architectural
Treatment

Cool, neutral grade. Shadows carry a navy cast; highlights stay clean. Contrast is firm but never crushed — detail must survive at both ends.

Composition

Architectural framing. Verticals stay vertical. Compose to the page grid and crop on the grid, using the 45° cut only where the image meets a coloured field.

People

Shown working, in correct PPE, at real installations. No posed handshakes, no arms folded in front of machinery, no stock smiles to camera.

Avoid

Generic server rooms, glowing blue interfaces, holographic overlays, composite “digital transformation” montages, and any image that could belong to any company in any sector.

Text over image

Only over a flat navy panel or a solid 70% navy scrim. Never directly on unmodified photography.

Krest Industrial Technologies26
KIT  /  Brand GuidelinesGraphic system

Layout and grid

Every KIT page is built on a twelve-column grid with a 15 mm outer margin and a 4 mm gutter. Twelve divides cleanly into halves, thirds, quarters and sixths, which covers every layout the system needs.

Content is placed on column boundaries without exception. Optical adjustment is permitted for type and marks; it is not permitted as a substitute for the grid.

Alignment principles

Titles sit in columns 1–3. Introductory text occupies columns 5–12 in one or two blocks. Content begins below a single hairline and runs to the foot margin.

Density

No more than three distinct content groups on a page. If a page needs a fourth, it is two pages.

Other formats

16:9 presentation and 1440 px web both use twelve columns with the same proportional margins. A4 portrait uses eight.

Industrial
applications

On plant, the identity has to survive powder coat, oil, abrasion and low light. Reproduction is single-colour more often than not, and the wordmark does the work.

The gradient is only reproduced by processes that can hold it — vinyl, digital print and powder-coat transfer. Everywhere else the monochrome master is used.

Operational
signage

Safety signage is governed by ISO 3864 and ISO 7010, not by this document. Shape, colour and symbol are mandated and must never be restyled to match the brand.

The brand appears alongside regulatory signage, never inside it. Wayfinding and facility signage are brand-led and use the Navy system.

Safety colours are specified by standard: mandatory blue, prohibition red, warning yellow, safe-condition green. They are legal requirements. Do not tint them toward Navy, do not substitute Gold for warning yellow, and do not apply the KIT logo inside a safety sign.

Where the brand does appear

On the sign carrier, the post or the surrounding board — adjacent to the regulatory panel and clearly separate from it.

Partnerships
and co-branding

In a partnership the two identities carry equal visual weight, separated by a vertical rule one cap height tall. KIT sits on the left in KIT-issued material and on the right in partner-issued material.

Weight is matched optically, not mathematically. Two logos of the same width can look very unequal; match the perceived mass of the marks.

Lockup pairing — light ground
Partner
Primary co-brand

Divider is 0.4 pt, one cap height tall, in Light Grey. Clear space of 1H applies outside the pair, not between the marks.

Lockup pairing — dark ground
Partner
Reversed

Both marks reverse. Where a partner mark cannot reverse, the pairing moves to a light ground.

Constrained pairing — wordmark only
Partner
Small format

Below 60 mm combined width, both parties reduce to their wordmark or symbol. The descriptor is never carried at this size.

Rules
Order

KIT leads on material it issues. The partner leads on material they issue. Alphabetical order applies to groups of three or more.

Separation

One vertical rule, one cap height tall, 0.4 pt. Never a slash, an ampersand, a plus sign or the accent shape.

Spacing

The gap between each mark and the rule is equal, and at least 1H.

Weight

Match optical mass, not bounding-box width. Adjust the KIT mark, never the partner's.

Colour

Both marks in full colour, or both monochrome. Never one of each.

Approval

Every co-branded lockup is approved by Marketing & Communications before release. No exceptions, including internal use.

Never

Do not merge the marks, overlap them, place one inside the other, create a joint symbol, or set a partner name in the KIT wordmark.
